external_source.title: Black Hole Formation in Failing Core-Collapse Supernovae
external_source.source_scope: Over 100 presupernova models studied with the spherically symmetric general-relativistic 1.5D GR1D code and simplified neutrino leakage/heating physics.
external_source.physical_quantity: xi_M = (M / M_sun) / (R(M_bary = M) / 1000 km); the paper focuses on xi_2.5 at bounce
external_source.locked_external_direction: Higher bounce compactness is associated with faster black-hole formation and progenitors that are harder to explode.
external_source.paper_boundary: The source itself treats compactness as a first-order predictor within a stated EOS and simplified 1.5D setup, not a universal one-parameter law.

verdict.label: PASS_EXTERNAL_QUALITATIVE_DIRECTIONAL_CONTACT__NO_PHYSICAL_PROMOTION
verdict.plain_language: Starbreaker's locked 3D density ladder moves in the same qualitative collapse direction as the frozen compactness result: more inward concentration produces more internal remnant and less ejecta.
verdict.strength: The ordering is strict in both aggregate ladders, all 42 individual anchor/seed ladders, all 42 same-total comparisons, and both exhaustive 24-permutation families.
verdict.limit: This is directional contact with an external simulation result, not a fit, measurement, physical calibration, black-hole prediction, or validation of the A packing law.
